newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner Bank rises on funds merger news.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner Bank rises on funds merger news.

text.p: Shares in Germany's third largest commercial bank Dresdner Bank rose to a year high on Friday encouraged by news that it plans to merge its global funds businesses.
Dresdner was up over three percent, or 1.30 marks, at 42.80 marks, having earlier touched a year high of 43 marks.
The fact that Dresdner shares had broken above its old year high of 41.85 marks was also a technical boost for the stock.
Meanwhile, the DAX index of 30 leading shares was almost one percent firmer, up 25.93 points at 2,739.15 at 1116 GMT.

Dresdner said it planned to merge its global funds business, comprising RCM Capital Management, Kleinwort Benson International Management and Thornton & Co into a global funds organisation led by RCM.

In a statement, Dresdner said the newly created organisation would manage assets of more than $50 billion worldwide outside of Germany and would accelerate Dresdner's drive to become a global funds management operator with a strong presence in the U.S., Europe and Asia.
Dealers said investors had already been recommending the stock for some time.
